title: La Barbe bleue - Blue Beard

full_text:
There lived once a nobleman of immense wealth, possessing splendid townhouses with marble terraces, carriages lined with gilded velvet, and services of solid gold and silver. Yet this lord was universally feared and shunned throughout the province because his beard was of an uncanny, midnight-blue hue, so grotesque that women and children trembled whenever he rode past.

Seeking a wife, Bluebeard paid court to the two fair daughters of a noble neighbor. Both maidens shrank from his suit, not only because of his dreadful beard, but because several wives had married him in years past, and not a single soul knew what had become of them. To soften their dread, Bluebeard invited the mother, daughters, and their friends to his opulent country chateau for an entire week of feasts, dances, hunting parties, and fireworks.

The entertainment was so enchanting that the younger daughter began to think his beard was not so blue after all, and that he was a most courteous gentleman. Soon after their return, the marriage was celebrated with great pomp.

A month later, Bluebeard informed his young wife that pressing affairs of state required him to journey to the distant provinces for six weeks. Handing her a massive iron ring carrying the keys to all his treasures, he said: 'Here are the keys to the grand wardrobes, the jewel vaults, the iron strongboxes of bullion, and the master keys that unlock every apartment in the palace. Make merry with your friends, spare no expense, and feast on whatever pleases your heart. But observe this small key of polished gold: it opens the low closet at the end of the long stone gallery on the ground floor. Open any chamber you wish, but I strictly forbid you to enter that closet. If you turn this key in its lock, expect my unyielding wrath.'

The young bride promised faithfully to respect his commandment, kissed him goodbye, and watched his carriage depart. Her companions flocked to the chateau, marveling at the silk tapestries, Venetian mirrors, and crystal chandeliers. Yet amidst their laughter, the bride could think of nothing but the forbidden closet. Driven by irresistible curiosity, she left her guests and hurried down the winding private stairs.

Reaching the secluded doorway, her hands trembled. She paused, remembering her husband's grave warning, but the burning desire to know conquered all prudence. She inserted the little golden key and turned the lock. The heavy door swung inward.

The chamber was dark and cold. As her eyes adjusted, she gasped in horror: the floor was strewn with dark stains, and within the shadowed alcoves lay the remains of Bluebeard's former wives, whom he had murdered for their curiosity. Paralyzed with terror, she dropped the golden key upon the flagstones. Picking it up with shaking fingers, she locked the door and fled to her private bedchamber.

Looking at the key, she noticed a stain of blood upon its polished tooth. She washed it with well water; she scrubbed it with scented soap; she rubbed it with pumice stone and emery powder. But the key was enchanted by dark sorcery: when the stain was cleansed from one side, it reappeared upon the other.

That very evening, Bluebeard returned unexpectedly, explaining that messengers had brought news settling his business favorably. He received his trembling wife with polite smiles, asking for his bunch of keys on the following morning. She surrendered them with pale cheeks, but the little golden key was missing.

'Where is the key to the closet at the gallery's end?' Bluebeard demanded, his brow darkening like thunder.

'I must have left it upon my dressing table, my lord,' she stammered.

'Bring it to me immediately,' he commanded.

When she placed the key in his palm, Bluebeard saw the crimson stain and sneered: 'How came this blood upon the metal? You entered the forbidden chamber, madam! Since you were so eager to see what lay within, you shall take your permanent place beside the ladies who came before you.'

The weeping bride fell at his feet, pleading for mercy with heartfelt tears. 'You must die,' Bluebeard roared, drawing his heavy steel scimitar.

'Grant me but seven minutes to say my prayers and commend my soul to heaven,' she begged.

'You have seven minutes,' growled the tyrant, 'and not a breath longer.'

Left alone, the young wife ran to the high stone turret where her sister Anne was watching the countryside. 'Anne, sister Anne!' she cried. 'Look out into the road and tell me if our two brothers are coming! They promised to visit us this morning!'

Sister Anne peered into the morning haze: 'I see only the sun making dust dance and the green grass growing.'

Below, Bluebeard shouted with a voice that shook the walls: 'Come down, madam, or I shall fetch you!'

'One moment more!' she begged, calling upward: 'Anne, sister Anne, do you see nothing coming?'

'I see a cloud of dust rising toward the east!' Anne called down. 'Alas, it is but a flock of sheep driven by a shepherd.'

'Your time has expired!' bellowed Bluebeard, his boots thundering up the stone stairs. He seized his wife by her golden hair, raising his blade to strike off her head.

At that desperate instant, the courtyard gates were battered down with a thunderous crash. Two mounted cavaliers—one a royal dragoon and the other a musketeer—dashed into the courtyard with drawn swords. Recognizing the bride's brothers, Bluebeard turned to flee, but the brave brothers pursued him across the terrace and ran him through with their blades, ending his reign of terror forever.

The young widow inherited the vast estates of Bluebeard. She provided an honorable dowry for sister Anne, purchased captaincies in the royal guard for her valiant brothers, and eventually married an honorable, noble gentleman whose kindness healed the memory of her ordeal, living out her days in peace, generosity, and joy.
moral: Curiosity indulged against wise counsel brings peril, but truth, courage, and family loyalty triumph over tyranny.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "La Barbe bleue - Blue Beard"?
options: Curiosity defeated wives, but also tale of female curiosity and male tyranny
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
